Explanation: The Luxury Listing is the Core Value Unit: a specific luxury product from a brand or boutique made globally discoverable and purchasable through the Farfetch customer experience.
Farfetch operates the luxury marketplace and customer interface. Coupang acquired the Farfetch business and assets in January 2024 and now reports Farfetch as part of its group.
Farfetch turns fragmented global luxury inventory into one searchable and transactional destination.
Aggregated demand and supply can generate marketplace economics while making the network more attractive to brands and boutiques.
Farfetch must coordinate premium customer experience, partner economics, cross-border fulfillment and platform profitability across a fragmented supply base.
Farfetch coordinates discovery, ordering, payment and commercial settlement around partner inventory.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Order / Pay — Luxury Customers place and pay for orders through Farfetch. | → Consumer · Discovery / Service — Farfetch provides global discovery, checkout and customer-service coordination. | ← Provider · Listing / Stock — Brands and boutiques provide product listings, inventory availability and commercial data. | → Provider · Demand / Payout — Farfetch routes customer demand to Providers and coordinates commercial proceeds. | ← Partner · Services — Commerce Services provide payments, logistics or technical capabilities. | → Partner · Volume / Fees — Farfetch's marketplace creates cross-border transaction and service volume for enabling partners.
